headline: This guy couldn't
body: His testosterone was normal. His bones were falling apart.
punch: And he was still growing as an adult.

headline: Last time
body: A man whose estrogen receptor didn't work never stopped growing. This is the other half of that experiment. Same outcome, different break in the chain.
punch: One couldn't read the signal. This one couldn't make it.

headline: He had aromatase deficiency
body: Aromatase turns androgens into estrogen. Without it, testosterone just stays testosterone. His androgen levels were normal to high and none of it became estradiol.

headline: The result
body: Unfused epiphyses. Open growth plates in an adult. And low bone mass, despite testosterone levels that should have built strong bone on their own.
punch: Normal androgens did not protect his skeleton.

headline: Then they gave him
body: Bone mineral density went up substantially. The deficit that normal testosterone completely failed to prevent got corrected by adding the hormone he couldn't produce.
punch: This is the treatment arm the receptor case could never have.

headline: Which is why
body: The receptor patient proved the signal is necessary. This one proved supplying it works, because his receptors were fine and only the supply was broken.
punch: Two natural experiments, opposite directions, same conclusion.

headline: So for male bone
body: Testosterone matters largely because of what it gets converted into. Estradiol looks necessary to maximise bone health in men, not optional.
punch: Androgen is the raw material. Estrogen does the work.

headline: The honest caveat
body: These are single patient case reports. Incredibly informative, because genetics isolates the variable instead of a study design doing it, but still n of one.
punch: Cleanest evidence available is not the same as biggest.

headline: It's never over
body: Real mechanisms, real citations, no protocols.
